title: Introduce goal-driven introspection: moeb compares goal criteria vs signal catalogue state to auto-generate gap signals
description: Given a machine-readable goal document (signal a1000041), moeb should be able to run an introspection pass that evaluates each goal criterion against the current signal catalogue — checking whether linked signals are resolved and whether unlinked criteria have any corresponding open or resolved signal coverage — then identifies gaps and produces draft signals to close them. The human reviews and approves proposed signals before they enter the catalogue. This inverts the current model where gap-finding is entirely human-driven and removes the dependency on the user noticing what is missing.
proposed_resolution: 1. Implement `moeb introspect` command and MCP tool equivalent. Inputs: `.moeb/goal.md`, the full signal catalogue. Outputs: (a) a goal health summary (N of M criteria satisfied), (b) a list of uncovered criteria with a draft signal JSON for each proposed gap, (c) criteria whose linked signals are all resolved (satisfied). 2. Proposed signals are written to `.moeb/signals/proposed/` as standard signal JSON files. They do not enter the catalogue or index.md until the human runs `moeb signal accept <id>`, which moves them into `catalogue/` and appends to `index.md`. 3. The conductor invokes the introspection loop automatically after each signal transitions to `resolved`, to surface newly-uncovered gaps without human prompting. 4. Include a `--suggest-goal-revisions` flag that outputs proposed additions or refinements to `.moeb/goal.md` criteria based on the pattern of recently-filed signals — i.e. moeb notices emerging themes and proposes new criteria. 5. Each proposed signal includes a `run_priority` hint derived from the number of unresolved goal criteria the gap affects.
